claims.text: Molecular dynamics simulations can be used to investigate the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at the atomic scale.
LAMMPS is an appropriate platform for simulating AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
An EAM or MEAM potential is suitable for the Au-Co-Cu-Ni-Pt system.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are disordered and in a high-entropy state.
The proposed intervention is heating or cooling the nanoparticles to various temperatures.
Representative simulation temperatures include 300 K and 1000 K.
Dislocation dynamics, lattice distortion, and atomic diffusion are structural mediators of the simulated thermal response.
The high-entropy nature of the nanoparticles and the identities of their constituent elements determine the proposed mechanism.
AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will exhibit enhanced thermal stability because of a high-entropy effect.
Heating or cooling may change dislocation dynamics and lattice distortion in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
The thermal behavior of individual Au, Co, Cu, Ni, or Pt materials or low-entropy alloys provides a proposed baseline.
The proposed simulation temperature range is approximately 300 K to 1500 K.
The proposed simulation time scale ranges from picoseconds to nanoseconds.
Results may be sensitive to the interatomic potential, simulation time scale, and boundary conditions.
Dislocation density, lattice distortion, and atomic diffusion coefficients can be measured in the proposed simulations.
A failure to observe enhanced stability or changes in dislocation dynamics would falsify the hypothesis.
